message.content:
Below is a ready‑to‑run **gcloud** command (the official CLI for Google Cloud) that creates a Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
If you prefer to hit the REST endpoint directly, I’ve also supplied the equivalent JSON payload for the `instances.insert` method.

---

## 1️⃣ Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1. Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create a new VM named “rtx-a6000-demo”
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# 3. Run the creation command
gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
    --project=$PROJECT_ID \
    --zone=$ZONE \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
    --subnet=default \
    --network-tier=PREMIUM \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --provisioning-model=STANDARD \
    --service-account=default@${PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
    --boot-disk-device-name=$INSTANCE_NAME \
    --no-shielded-secure-boot \
    --no-shielded-vtpm \
    --no-shielded-integrity-monitoring \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: add a startup script
    --accelerator=count=1,type=nvidia-tesla-a6000 \
    --reservation-affinity=any
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration (`n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM). |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Sets a 100 GB balanced SSD boot disk. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU. |
| `--reservation-affinity` | Allows the instance to use any available GPU reservation (useful if you have pre‑emptible GPUs). |

> **Tip:** If you’re using a custom VPC or firewall rules, replace `--subnet=default` and `--network-tier=PREMIUM` with your own values.

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Call (JSON)

If you’d rather use the raw REST endpoint, here’s the minimal JSON body you can POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y python3-pip"
      }
    ]
  },
  "reservationAffinity": {
    "consumeReservationType": "ANY_RESERVATION"
  }
}
```

Send this payload to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json
```

Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and any other placeholders with your actual values.

---

### Quick Checklist

- [ ] Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your real project ID.
- [ ] Verify that the `us-central1-a` region has available RTX A6000 GPUs (you can check via the console or `gcloud compute accelerator-types list`).
- [ ] Ensure you have the necessary IAM permissions (`roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` and `roles/compute.acceleratorUser`).

Once executed, the VM will spin up, attach the GPU, and boot into Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. You can SSH into it with:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh rtx-a6000-demo --project=$PROJECT_ID --zone=$ZONE
```

Happy GPU computing!
